items.text: A 25-year-old citizen was arrested in the Kalachay district of Rudsar for posting content on social media. The Rudsar police commander stated that the charges are insult and public disturbance.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, met with Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General, in New York on Friday, October 3. Before the negotiations, he signed the UN memorial book. Pezeshkian traveled to New York to attend the 81st UN General Assembly.

Shahbaz Sharif stated that Pakistan brought Washington and Tehran together for negotiations through diplomatic efforts. He discussed the Middle East crisis and its impacts on lives, economy, and shipping routes. He also condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

Majid Roshannejad, a political prisoner in Tehran's Great Prison, is deprived of specialized medical care due to his neurological and psychiatric illness. He is held in ward four without separation according to crime type and faces harassment. Authorities prevent his transfer to external medical centers.

Adidas unveiled a special jersey for Argentina's national football team for Lionel Messi's farewell match. Messi will wear the number 10 jersey for the last time on October 6 in a friendly match against Benin. This match marks the end of Messi's international football career.

Shida Saberi, a resident of Shiraz, was arrested by security police officers on Sunday, 29th of Shahrivar. She was transferred to Adelabad prison in Shiraz. This news was reported by HRANA news agency.

The Scottish prosecution announced that the 34-year-old Iranian man detained while attempting to enter the UK's nuclear submarine base is currently not being prosecuted. He was arrested along with a Romanian woman in March 2026. The case may be pursued if further evidence is found.

A citizen reported in a video to Iran International that GPS is down and the internet is weak on the route from Isfahan to Tehran. He says this situation makes driving very difficult. This problem is ongoing.

The Prime Minister of Qatar described the situation in the Strait of Hormuz as very difficult and challenging. He said the security of this international waterway is at risk and ship passage is problematic. He called for an end to the use of waterways for pressure and extortion.

The Court of Appeals of Qom Province confirmed the sentences of lashes and artistic activity bans for Parasto Ahmadi and eight other members involved in the Caravanserai concert. Previously, they were sentenced to 74 lashes, two years of travel ban, and two years of prohibition from artistic activities. The verdict was initially issued by the criminal court.

Nawaf Salam, the Prime Minister of Lebanon, stated at the United Nations that attacks by the Islamic Republic threaten regional security and maritime navigation. He said the consequences extend beyond conflicts, affecting supply chains, commodity prices, and inflation rates. These remarks were made on Friday, September 24.

Masoud Pezeshkian appreciated Xi Jinping's support for returning to the Islamabad agreement and resolving disputes through dialogue. He emphasized that the Islamic Republic seeks to implement agreed commitments and serious negotiations. He also noted the alignment of Tehran and Beijing's views on respecting national sovereignty and maintaining regional stability.
The audio version of Harf Akhar with Pouria Zeraati has been released. The topic covers details of the US plan to resume attacks. This was reported by Iran International.

The Tehran prosecutor's office has filed a legal case against the cast of the play "Tehran/Paris/Tehran/Bridge." This action followed the release of images from the play's performance. The images showed Fatemeh Masoudifar and Mehrdad Sedighian performing a scene.

A citizen reported that children's play equipment was removed from the park in Payam Town, Karaj. In its place, an anonymous cemetery was established. Additionally, a Hosseiniyeh for Basijis was built nearby.

The dormitory of the Zarrineh boys' boarding high school in Divandareh has been used as a military base since Esfand 1404. This has deprived students, especially those from nearby villages, of access to the dormitory. Consequently, the education of some students has been disrupted due to the difficulty of daily commuting.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, during a meeting with his Indian counterpart in New York, said that Iran and Oman have negotiated an agreement to create a safe shipping route in the Strait of Hormuz. He added that he briefed the Indian foreign minister on the latest status of these talks. Araghchi also blamed US actions against Iran's commercial shipping as the main source of insecurity in the region and the Strait of Hormuz.

Kaveh Madani, head of the Water, Environment, and Health Institute at the United Nations University, described the water crisis as a new axis for global cooperation. He emphasized that the water issue has become a concern beyond developing countries, reaching Europe and North America. Madani warned that using water as a tool for political pressure could increase tensions.

Danny Danon, Israel's ambassador to the UN, said Israel desires and hopes for a regime change in Iran. He added that this is not the official goal of Israel's military operations but would benefit the people of Iran and the region. He also mentioned that regional countries like Bahrain and the UAE have taken a firm stance against the Islamic Republic.

Fereshteh Pezeshk said that both the US and Israel want to change the government in Iran but have different views on how to achieve it. She added that Israel alone cannot remove the Islamic Republic. Trump is trying to impose his demands on the Islamic Republic, but the ultimate goal of the US remains unclear.

Abbas Araghchi announced that Iran has presented a specific seven-day plan to the US for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The final decision on this plan rests with Washington. Araghchi added that the necessary actions were previously included in the June agreement between the two countries.

The French national football team defeated Turkey in their first match under Zinedine Zidane's coaching. Kylian Mbappe scored in the 54th minute but was injured in his left knee and was substituted. France had several scoring opportunities, while Turkey also created some chances to equalize.

The Italian national football team lost 2-0 to Belgium in the first week of the UEFA Nations League. The goals were scored by Michy Batshuayi and Romelu Lukaku. After the match, a verbal altercation occurred between Gianluigi Donnarumma and Romelu Lukaku.
In the audio version 24 with Fardad Farahzad, the criticism of Lebanon and Iraq against the Islamic Republic was discussed.

The chiefs of staff of Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey held a meeting in Riyadh emphasizing their commitment to collective defense of Saudi Arabia's security and territorial integrity. They condemned attacks on Mecca and Saudi Arabia's civilian infrastructure. They also discussed expanding intelligence and military cooperation to strengthen collective defense.

The Qom appellate court confirmed the conviction of Parasto Ahmadi and eight others involved in the Caravanserai concert. In the initial trial, these artists were sentenced to 74 lashes, two years of travel ban, and two years of prohibition from artistic activities. The appellate court's ruling remained unchanged.

Kambiz Tavana said the reaction of Iranian officials to the flight suspensions has been mostly threatening. US sanctions pressure may force regional airlines to stop cooperating with Iran. China's position remains unclear and may be influenced by recent talks between Trump and Xi Jinping.

The spokesperson of the IRGC stated that the Islamic Republic will continue to punish the US until its seven conditions are met. He said Iran's missiles can destroy the US multilayered defenses. Also, control of the Strait of Hormuz is in the hands of the IRGC Navy, and passage through the strait is now limited to oil from Iran's trading partners.

Mohammad Qaedi said China is unlikely to guarantee the implementation of any agreement between Iran and the US because Beijing-Washington relations go beyond the Iran issue. He added that until the final decision-maker in Tehran is clear, China's effective role will be difficult. Qaedi also said Iran's leverage in the Strait of Hormuz will erode over time, complicating nuclear negotiations if no agreement is reached.

Shahram Kholdi said Israel, as the only democracy in the Middle East, plays an important role in removing the Islamic Republic. He added that the disagreement between the US and Israel is about how to change the government in Iran, not the principle of change. The US prefers change from within the government, while Israel views all factions of the Islamic Republic as a single structure.

Hossein Abdi, the coach of Iran's under-23 team, did not deny his relationship with Ali Akbar Raefipour and described it with pride. Raefipour is known as a government speaker with statements about Mahdism, the end times, and hostility towards Israel. This topic was covered in Raha Pourbakhsh's report on the Hattrick program.

Mazdak Mirzaei discussed the elimination of Iran's under-23 team from the Nagoya Asian Games on the Hattrick program. He criticized the selection of Hossein Abdi as a negative point in Iranian football, stating that Abdi reached the position through connections and flattery. He also mentioned the unclear background of Abdi's assistants.

Hossein Abdi, the coach of Iran's under-23 team, has not denied his relationship with Ali Akbar Raefipour and has spoken about it. Raefipour is known for his statements about Mahdism and hostility towards Israel. This relationship is questionable in the process of Abdi's appointment to lead Iran's youth football teams.

Ata Mohamad said groups close to the Islamic Republic in Iraq may increase pressure on the Baghdad government to lift restrictions and resume Iran flights. This pressure could range from sit-ins at airports to broader actions. There is also a possibility of more radical measures if the negotiation deadlock continues.

The Canadian government has shifted its approach at the UN General Assembly, focusing on regional maritime security instead of human rights violations in Iran. This change has raised concerns about weakening Ottawa's 20-year role in advancing annual human rights resolutions against the Islamic Republic. The report is by Mahsa Mortazavi, a journalist from Iran International.

Molavi Abdolhamid emphasized the remembrance of the bloody Fridays of Zahedan and Khash, marking the fourth anniversary. He described the shooting by security forces at protesters as very shocking and heartbreaking. The incident occurred on October 8, 2022, resulting in many worshippers killed and injured.

The Wall Street Journal, citing American officials, reported that Trump rejected the Islamic Republic's proposal for a seven-day ceasefire. According to the proposal, in exchange for the US lifting the blockade of Iranian ports, the Strait of Hormuz would be reopened and nuclear negotiations resumed. Pezeshkian had said that if the US accepts this proposal, its implementation will begin immediately.

The Saudi-led coalition announced it intercepted two ballistic missiles and two drones launched by the Houthis. The missiles were headed toward Khamis Mushait and the drones toward Riyadh. Saudi civil defense issued warnings for Khamis Mushait and Abha but not for Riyadh.

The Wall Street Journal, citing American officials, reported that the US president rejected the Islamic Republic's proposal for a seven-day ceasefire and told aides he expects to resume bombing after the November midterm elections. The proposal included reopening the Strait of Hormuz and resuming nuclear talks in exchange for lifting the US blockade of Iranian ports.

Rayan Fihi, the lawyer of Reza Valizadeh, reported that his client's physical condition has worsened and he is struggling to breathe. He also mentioned the concerning conditions in Evin prison following the Israeli attack. Valizadeh stated in an audio message that he chose prison over cooperating with the IRGC intelligence organization.

The Washington Post reported, citing US officials, that classified documents containing US intelligence community assessments show that Saudi Arabia has not ruled out the option of developing a nuclear weapons program. This assessment has increased concerns among a number of US lawmakers about the Trump administration's deal to help launch Saudi Arabia's civilian nuclear program. A group of Democratic senators warned that the deal could give Riyadh the ability to enrich uranium.

Fatemeh Jami, a resident of Gorgan, has been detained in the city's prison for about three months. She is accused of insulting sacred values and communicating with opposition groups. No trial has been held for her yet.

Kayhan newspaper criticized Masoud Pezeshkian's remarks in New York, stating that revenge is a divine mission and killers should not feel safe. The newspaper demanded justice for the martyred Imam and the execution of Trump. Kayhan rejected Pezeshkian's statements about the Iranian government's lack of intent to assassinate Trump.

The head of the Central Province Road Police reported the overturning of a passenger bus. In this incident, 11 people died and 24 were injured. The cause of the accident was stated to be driver fatigue and drowsiness.

Ebrahim Rezaei, a member of the National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, said not to beg for agreement and understanding. He added that such an approach from the other side is seen as a sign of weakness. This will lead to continued pressure on the Islamic Republic.

Shayan Samiei stated that the Islamic Republic intends to use the Strait of Hormuz as a means for economic breathing and aims to convert the leverage of crisis creation into economic advantage by proposing its reopening in exchange for reduced blockade. He added that the main issue is the credibility of the Islamic Republic's commitments, and China evaluates its support based on cost and benefit. Beijing does not consider the Islamic Republic as an insurance for survival and may easily move on if its interests change.

Pegah Bani Hashemi pointed to the situation of political prisoners and harsh sentences against protesters. She said the statements of Iranian officials at the United Nations differ from the real conditions in Iran and the demands of a large part of society. These remarks address the human rights situation in Iran.

The Iranian women's national kabaddi team lost to India 37-34 in the final of the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya and won the silver medal. In the previous edition, Iran lost to India in the semifinals. India is one of the strongest kabaddi teams in the world.

Quds newspaper called for accountability over the cancellation of Iranian flights by neighboring countries, stating that making air corridors unsafe does not require direct military action, as navigation warnings, drills, continuous NOTAMs, and increased flight risk are sufficient. The newspaper added that reports indicate regional airports are complying with US sanctions, leading to Iran's air isolation, and that any blockade of the country means war and demands an equivalent response.

The Iraqi government is in direct talks with the US to exempt some of its airports from US Treasury sanctions against Iranian flights. The negotiations aim to resume flights for humanitarian reasons such as medical treatment, education, and religious travel. Iraq also emphasized efforts to reduce tensions and end conflicts through dialogue.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said that the Islamic Republic is not seeking a comprehensive agreement with the US and that its goal in creating pauses is to buy time. He added that prolonging the process could give the Islamic Republic the opportunity to maintain its missile and nuclear capabilities and adjust to future conditions. This situation also facilitates increased intervention by China and Russia.

Zinedine Zidane announced that Kylian Mbappe must leave the French national team camp due to a knee injury. Mbappe was injured during the match against Turkey and will miss France's next three games. The French Football Federation confirmed that Mbappe will return to Madrid for treatment.

Rouhollah Rahimpour referred to Nawaf Salam's remarks about the monopoly of weapons by the Lebanese government, stating that Lebanon and Iraq are moving towards a model where decisions of war and peace are controlled by governments. He added that this trend could challenge the influence model of the Islamic Republic and parallel armed forces. If official support channels close, the IRGC may move towards smaller, more informal, and deniable networks.

France has decided to send military forces and defense equipment to Saudi Arabia. The mission aims to protect the Yanbu oil terminal. Details about the number of troops and types of defense systems have not yet been announced.

The spokesperson of Iran's Ministry of Defense announced that part of the military and strategic capabilities have been deployed in underground infrastructures. This has prevented the enemy from accurately assessing Iran's defense capacity and weapons production. Recent wars have been hybrid, involving social, economic, and media domains as well.

The major European leagues including the English Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, and Bundesliga have demanded fundamental reforms in FIFA's management structure. They accused Gianni Infantino of promoting exploitative ideas. They also called for increased oversight of disciplinary cases to prevent political interference.

Zartosht Ahmadi Ragheb, a political prisoner in Karaj Central Prison, was sentenced to one year of imprisonment. Additionally, he was banned from leaving the country and removed from public and government services for two years. This sentence was issued by the Karaj Revolutionary Court.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin from Iran International said political disagreements in the Islamic Republic over negotiations with the US and regional countries have intensified. He identified the main problem as the lack of a common language among factions. The absence of a unified policy has caused confusion and increased internal criticism.

Hossein Ali Hajideligani stated that places from which flights or missiles are launched against the Islamic Republic should be targeted. He emphasized that the palaces of the sheikhdoms and kings in the Persian Gulf region should be targeted. He also mentioned that the impeachment plan for the president is currently only a discussion.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated that the US and Israel seek to control regional wealth by creating divisions among Muslim countries. He said the developments in Yemen are unrelated to the Islamic Republic and emphasized resolving disputes through dialogue. He also mentioned that the Islamic Republic no longer trusts negotiations with the US due to repeated attacks and sanctions, but Qatar and Pakistan are mediating.

Mehdi Taj announced that Hossein Abdi's resignation was accepted after the under-23 Iranian team's elimination in the Asian Games. He also stated that friendly matches for the senior national team are not meant to avoid losses but to prepare for official competitions. The Football Federation has provided the best conditions for the national teams.

The second part of the documentary series Amran Keshvar will cover Kurdistan, Kermanshah, and West Azerbaijan. It will be broadcast on Saturday at 17:46 and 21:45 Tehran time. The broadcast will be on Iran International.

The head of the Dasht-e Azadegan Environmental Protection Office stated that 35% of the Hoor al-Azim wetland currently has water, while 65 to 70% is dry. He emphasized that the wetland's water rights must be permanently ensured. With the forecast of increased rainfall, there is hope to use floods to supply water to the wetland.

Mohsen Heydari stated that Mojtaba Khamenei was injured in the attacks on the leadership office on Esfand 9. He added that three hospitals in Tehran were bombed after the incident, and Mojtaba Khamenei was in the third hospital. Heydari also said that Mojtaba Khamenei is healthy and capable of leadership.

Siamak Mirzaei and Ali Vasaghi, two Turk activists, have been held in Ardabil prison for 91 days without judicial decision. They have been denied access to a lawyer since their arrest. Their families have not succeeded in obtaining permission for their temporary release.

Asieh Amini stated that the flogging sentence and activity ban for the Caravanserai concert organizers have been confirmed. Additionally, charges have been filed against theater organizers in Tehran. She said the Islamic Republic uses religious and judicial laws to control artists.

Sepideh Gholian announced that a death sentence has been issued for Mahbubeh Shabani, a political prisoner in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. Shabani previously went on a hunger strike protesting prison conditions and has been deprived of visits and phone calls. She has also suffered from a skin disease and has been transferred multiple times between different prison wards.

Hojat Karimi, a member of the Football Federation board, announced his and others' opposition to a 4-year contract extension for Amir Ghalenoei. He also expressed concerns about bonus payments and contract renewal conditions. The Football Federation has not yet commented on the matter.

Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social that Iran cannot have nuclear weapons. Earlier, it was reported that Trump rejected the Islamic Republic's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz for seven days. These statements were published on Saturday.

Shahbaz Sharif, Prime Minister of Pakistan, warned at the UN General Assembly that conflicts are dangerously escalating. He emphasized that the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab should not become choke points of confrontation. These waterways should bring promises of prosperity, not the dangers of war.

The conference 'Human Rights Crisis in Iran; From Common Principles to Common Action' is being held at the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo. Iran International reporter Mehran Abbasian spoke with Nasser Bolidei, Secretary-General of the Balochistan People's Party, on the sidelines of the conference.

Mahbubeh Shabani, a detainee from the December 2025 protests, was sentenced to death by the first branch of the Revolutionary Court in Mashhad. She was accused of operational actions to strengthen Israel, the USA, and opposition groups. The death sentence has been communicated to her defense lawyer.

The Secretariat of the Supreme National Security Council announced that the Islamic Republic will not take military retaliatory action in response to recent restrictions on air transportation. Negotiations with the relevant countries to lift these restrictions are ongoing. Several non-military measures for retaliation exist and will be applied if necessary.

Tasnim reported that no technical delegation from the Islamic Republic traveled to New York to negotiate with the United States. The agency called the reports about such a delegation's trip media fabrication. Abbas Araghchi and his accompanying delegation will return to Iran on Tuesday as scheduled.

The Iranian embassy in Bogota announced that consular services will continue until the last day of the embassy's operation. The Colombian government accused Tehran of possible ties to terrorist groups. Reza Pahlavi appreciated Colombia's decision to cut ties with Iran.

Zahra Zarei finished second in the women's 400m final at the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya with a time of 52.38 seconds, winning the silver medal. This is the first medal for Iranian women in track events at the Asian Games.

Homayoun Falakshahi stated that no new oil shipments from Iran have been recorded this month. New oil exports from Iran have reached zero, and floating oil reserves are decreasing. It is predicted that most of these reserves will be depleted within two to three weeks.

A video shows that on Saturday, October 4th, military forces with vehicles equipped with loudspeakers attended a school in northern Tehran and played religious chants. Some viewers expressed concern about the military presence and government programs in schools. They believe these actions may associate the school environment with political coercion and a security atmosphere.

Babak Roshanzamir, a citizen from Likak, was arrested on Friday, September 27, and transferred to Dehdasht prison. He was arrested after visiting the martyrs' cemetery in Likak and lighting a candle in their memory. This information is based on reports received by Iran International.

Students of Razi University in Kermanshah went on a hunger strike on Saturday, October 4th, protesting the poor quality and unsanitary conditions of the university food. They refused to eat the university food. This action was taken to protest the unfavorable food conditions.

In a meeting in Bushehr province, teachers were asked to monitor and report students' political or critical remarks. Authorities warned that failure to report could lead to teachers' arrest. This comes amid increasing involvement of military and security institutions in schools across the country.

Pope Leo XIV held a mass at Place de la Concorde in Paris on the second day of his visit. Approximately 600,000 people gathered in the square and surrounding streets to see him. This report was published by Sajedeh Sharifi from Iran International.

Iranians in Sweden held a rally and march on Saturday in support of the national revolution and Prince Reza Pahlavi. A video of this event was sent to Iran International. The gathering demonstrated support for the national revolution.

In schools of Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari province, managers require students to pay for receiving plaques and have made school contributions mandatory. The Yasuj spare parts dealers' guild went on strike and gathered in front of the governor's office on Saturday, October 4. Reports also mention increased prices and decreased food quality at Kurdistan University and the presence of law enforcement forces in Tabriz.

Donald Trump stated that he received a proposal from the Islamic Republic for the immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz but rejected it. He said the US has full control over the Strait and a large volume of oil passes through it. Trump does not oppose the idea of an agreement but found the proposed deal unacceptable.

Fatemeh Mohitizadeh was disqualified from the heptathlon at the Nagoya Asian Games due to using unauthorized shoes. The Iranian Athletics Federation protested this decision, stating her shoes were approved before the competition. The National Olympic Committee said the responsibility for equipment inspection lies with the athlete and coaching staff.

The Qom Court of Appeals confirmed the sentence of 74 lashes for Parasto Ahmadi and eight other musicians involved in the Caravanserai concert. In addition to lashes, they were sentenced to two years of prohibition from audiovisual activities and travel bans. The sentence was issued on charges of offending public decency through producing and publishing indecent content online.

At least 20 people died in two separate road accidents in Iran. A bus overturned on the Hamedan-Saveh highway, killing 11 and injuring 24. Additionally, a collision between a bus and a truck on the Birjand-Ghaen road resulted in 9 deaths and 5 injuries.

At the end of the seventh day of the 2026 Nagoya Asian Games, Iranian athletes won one gold and three silver medals, and Iran's position in the medal table remained seventh. Hamedreza Tayebi won a gold medal in discus throw, while Iran's national men's and women's kabaddi teams and Zahra Zarei in the 400-meter race won silver medals.

Sardar Ramin, a resident of Qarneh village in Naqadeh, was arrested one week ago. There is still no information about his whereabouts or condition. His family and relatives remain unaware of his status.

Amnesty International has released an unprecedented report on the crackdowns during the Mahsa uprising. The report focuses especially on the three provinces of Kurdistan, Kermanshah, and West Azerbaijan. These provinces had the highest number of casualties during the Mahsa uprising.

Shayan Samiei commented on the Islamic Republic's plan for the immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. He said the Islamic Republic aims to turn the strait into an economic lifeline and convert the crisis leverage into an economic advantage. He also pointed out the credibility of the Islamic Republic's commitments, which Tehran has repeatedly failed to uphold.

Abbas Tahsin Saeed Al-Amari, an Iraqi national, has been held in Evin prison for over 9 months without a clear status. His case is being reviewed in Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. He is accused of propaganda against the regime and espionage for a foreign government.

Fardad Farahzad, a reporter from Iran International, asked Abbas Araghchi about hopes for an agreement and the possibility of renewed war, but he did not respond. Majid Takht-Ravanchi was also questioned about negotiations with the US and his avoidance of media interviews, but he remained silent. Both passed by the reporter without answering.

Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, Bahrain's Foreign Minister, stated that the Gulf countries and Jordan have been targeted by nearly seven thousand attacks by Iran. These attacks included ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones, targeting civilian infrastructure and ports. He also mentioned the death of 22 sailors and the laying of mines in international shipping routes.

Abbas Araghchi and Majid Takht-Ravanchi did not answer journalists' questions about negotiations and the possibility of an agreement in front of the UN building. They continued on their way without responding. This was reported by an Iran International journalist.

The Iran Trade Development Organization announced that the import of home appliances from South Korea is now allowed without restrictions. This ban, imposed five years ago by Ali Khamenei's order, has been lifted. The new decision was made based on the resolutions of the Border Trade Regulation Working Group.

Seyed Ali Mousavi was transferred to Sheiban Prison in Ahvaz to serve the remainder of his six-year sentence. He had previously served about 18 months and was released for medical treatment. Recently, he was summoned to continue serving his sentence.
The Afghanistan delegation ended the eighth day of the 2026 Asian Games without winning any medals. This report was provided by Mehdi Kazemi from Iran International.

The US federal prosecutor announced that Reza Dindar, a 44-year-old Iranian citizen, has been sentenced to 18 months in prison for participating in a scheme to illegally transfer sensitive US equipment and technology to Iran via China. According to a statement from the US Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Washington, he was also sentenced to pay a $10,000 fine and three years of supervised release. Dindar was first indicted in August 2014, arrested in Panama in July 2025 at the US request, extradited to the US in April 2026, and pleaded guilty just six weeks later.

Morteza Parvin Joda, a political prisoner of Azerbaijani origin, suffers from severe back pain, migraine, and toothache and has been deprived of proper medical care. Despite paying for treatment costs, prison officials have only prescribed painkillers and have not taken effective action for transfer or specialist examination. His condition has been confirmed by informed sources.

Alireza Dabir, the head of the Football Federation, called for the system to make a clear decision about football and said the future of football must be clarified. He emphasized that the federation, Ministry of Sports, and other institutions should decide on football's future. Mehdi Mohammad Nabi, the deputy head of the federation, responded by saying Dabir should focus on his own work.

Faisal bin Farhan, Saudi Arabia's foreign minister, called on the international community at the UN General Assembly to confront Iran's threats to regional security and to restore the status of the Strait of Hormuz without restrictions. He emphasized that Saudi Arabia and regional countries have been targeted by Iranian attacks and stressed their right to protect national security. The foreign minister described Gulf security as integral to global security.

Siamak Javadi said the sharp decline in China's oil imports from Iran indicates that Beijing does not consider the Islamic Republic a strategic partner. Iran's economy is facing challenges due to reduced foreign currency revenues, inflation, and structural crises. The return of most oil exports from the Strait of Hormuz has weakened the Islamic Republic's leverage.

Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, Bahrain's Foreign Minister, stated that the country has rejected any plan for permits or fees for passage through the Strait of Hormuz. He emphasized that the Strait of Hormuz is an international waterway and the right of passage cannot be conditional. He also warned that using international waterways as economic pressure tools is dangerous.

Three workers died in an olive processing unit in Gilvan, Tarom, due to an accident caused by unsafe working conditions. The lack of workplace safety and poor conditions were cited as the reasons for the incident.

Navid Mohibi said the three-hour negotiations between Tehran and Washington in New York were unsuccessful. Disagreements remain over lifting the blockade, oil sales, returning blocked funds, and the Lebanon crisis. He suggested a direct confrontation may occur after the midterm elections.

Hassan Ali Akhlaqi Amiri, a member of the Iranian parliament's Cultural Commission, said that the ban on Iranian airline flights in Iraq could harm bilateral relations and called on Iraqi officials not to follow US policies in this matter. He said that imposing restrictions on these routes will directly affect communication between the two countries. He added that the ban is not befitting the Iraqi nation and could harm the long-standing and extensive ties between Iran and Iraq.

27 economists and economic activists warned about the deepening crisis if the war and naval blockade continue. Donya-e-Eqtesad quoted an economist saying the ongoing situation could lead to social protests. This issue was discussed in an interview with Ashkan Nezamabadi.
